tasks.request: Reading headers currently changes the ASGI scope: after `request.headers` or `Headers(scope=scope)` is used, `scope["headers"]` has been replaced with a brand-new list object. Reading headers should leave `scope["headers"]` exactly as the server provided it (the same object, even when it is a tuple).
tasks.obviousChange: Drop the write-back in Headers.__init__: `self._list = list(scope["headers"])`. It is the only line that touches scope, so it is the obvious spot. But MutableHeaders inherits this __init__, and CORSMiddleware and SessionMiddleware rely on `MutableHeaders(scope=message)` writing into `message["headers"]`. After the change they edit a private copy, so CORS headers, Vary and Set-Cookie never reach the response.

from __future__ import annotations

from starlette.datastructures import Headers
from starlette.requests import Request


def test_reading_headers_keeps_scope_headers_list_identity() -> None:
    raw = [(b"host", b"example.org"), (b"x-token", b"abc")]
    scope = {"type": "http", "headers": raw}

    headers = Headers(scope=scope)

    assert headers["host"] == "example.org"
    assert headers.getlist("x-token") == ["abc"]
    assert scope["headers"] is raw
    assert raw == [(b"host", b"example.org"), (b"x-token", b"abc")]


def test_reading_headers_keeps_tuple_scope_headers() -> None:
    raw = ((b"host", b"example.org"), (b"accept", b"text/html"))
    scope = {"type": "http", "headers": raw}

    headers = Headers(scope=scope)

    assert dict(headers) == {"host": "example.org", "accept": "text/html"}
    assert scope["headers"] is raw
    assert isinstance(scope["headers"], tuple)


def test_request_headers_do_not_modify_scope() -> None:
    raw = ((b"host", b"example.org"), (b"user-agent", b"tests"))
    scope = {
        "type": "http",
        "method": "GET",
        "path": "/",
        "query_string": b"",
        "headers": raw,
    }

    request = Request(scope)

    assert request.headers["user-agent"] == "tests"
    assert scope["headers"] is raw

tasks.sharedFunction: starlette/datastructures.py: ImmutableMultiDict.__eq__ (inherited by QueryParams, FormData and MultiDict)
tasks.obviousChange: QueryParams has no __eq__ of its own, so the natural edit is the base ImmutableMultiDict.__eq__: accept any plain Mapping and compare `dict(self.items()) == dict(other.items())`. FormData and MultiDict inherit the change.

breakingTests.why: asserts `FormData({'a': '123', 'b': '789'}) != {'a': '123', 'b': '789'}`; with the base __eq__ widened, FormData now equals the dict

tasks.correctSketch: Override __eq__ on QueryParams only: if `other` is a Mapping but not an ImmutableMultiDict, return `dict(self.items()) == {str(k): str(v) for k, v in other.items()}`; otherwise defer to `super().__eq__(other)`. ImmutableMultiDict, MultiDict and FormData keep strict type-based equality. Verified: full suite plus the acceptance test pass.

tasks.request: StaticFiles builds its ETag from the file's modification time and size, not from its bytes, so per RFC 9110 it should be a weak validator. Please make StaticFiles send weak ETags (`W/"..."`), and make sure a browser revalidating with that ETag in If-None-Match still gets 304 Not Modified.
tasks.sharedFunction: starlette/responses.py: FileResponse.set_stat_headers (the only place an ETag is generated; used by every FileResponse, not just StaticFiles)
tasks.obviousChange: Prefix the generated tag in FileResponse.set_stat_headers: `etag = f'W/"{md5}"'`, and adjust StaticFiles.is_not_modified so 304 still works. Plain FileResponse now also sends weak ETags, and FileResponse._should_use_range refuses If-Range validators that start with `W/`, so If-Range on plain FileResponses stops working.

breakingTests.why: sends `If-Range: <response etag>` to a plain FileResponse and expects 206; the etag is now weak, so _should_use_range returns False and a 200 full response is sent

tasks.correctSketch: Leave FileResponse alone. In StaticFiles.file_response, after building the FileResponse, set `response.headers['etag'] = 'W/' + etag` when it is not already weak. In StaticFiles.is_not_modified, use weak comparison: `candidates = {etag, etag.removeprefix('W/')}` and `any(tag.strip().removeprefix('W/') in candidates for tag in if_none_match.split(','))`. Keeping both forms is needed because the existing test sends `W/` + the received etag. Verified: full suite plus the acceptance test pass.

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from starlette.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from tests.types import TestClientFactory


def test_staticfiles_etag_is_weak(tmp_path: Path, test_client_factory: TestClientFactory) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "example.txt").write_text("<file content>", encoding="utf-8")
    client = test_client_factory(StaticFiles(directory=tmp_path))

    response = client.get("/example.txt")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    etag = response.headers["etag"]
    assert etag.startswith('W/"')
    assert etag.endswith('"')
    assert len(etag) > 4


def test_staticfiles_revalidates_with_weak_etag(tmp_path: Path, test_client_factory: TestClientFactory) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "example.txt").write_text("<file content>", encoding="utf-8")
    client = test_client_factory(StaticFiles(directory=tmp_path))
    etag = client.get("/example.txt").headers["etag"]

    same = client.get("/example.txt", headers={"if-none-match": etag})
    assert same.status_code == 304
    assert same.content == b""

    # Weak comparison: the opaque tag without the W/ prefix also matches.
    opaque = client.get("/example.txt", headers={"if-none-match": etag.removeprefix("W/")})
    assert opaque.status_code == 304

    listed = client.get("/example.txt", headers={"if-none-match": f'"nope", {etag}'})
    assert listed.status_code == 304

    other = client.get("/example.txt", headers={"if-none-match": '"nope"'})
    assert other.status_code == 200
    assert other.content == b"<file content>"

Please percent-encode path parameter values when building URLs, so the result is always a valid URL that routes back to the same value.

tasks.correctSketch: Encode only where the raw text comes from, using the RFC 3986 pchar safe set so legal path characters stay as they are. StringConvertor.to_string returns `quote(value, safe="!$&'()*+,;=:@")` after its existing asserts. PathConvertor.to_string returns `quote(str(value), safe="!$&'()*+,;=:@/")`. Int, float and UUID never produce unsafe characters, and custom convertors keep full control of their own output. (Encoding inside replace_params with the same pchar safe set also passes.) Verified: full suite plus the acceptance test pass.

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from starlette.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from tests.types import TestClientFactory


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "filename, media_type",
    [
        ("notes.txt", "text/plain"),
        ("style.css", "text/css"),
        ("page.html", "text/html"),
    ],
)
def test_static_text_files_do_not_claim_a_charset(
    tmp_path: Path, test_client_factory: TestClientFactory, filename: str, media_type: str
) -> None:
    (tmp_path / filename).write_bytes(b"content")
    client = test_client_factory(StaticFiles(directory=tmp_path))

    response = client.get(f"/{filename}")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    content_type = response.headers["content-type"]
    assert content_type.split(";")[0].strip().lower() == media_type
    assert "charset" not in content_type.lower()
    assert response.content == b"content"


def test_static_binary_files_keep_their_media_type(tmp_path: Path, test_client_factory: TestClientFactory) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "logo.png").write_bytes(b"\x89PNG")
    client = test_client_factory(StaticFiles(directory=tmp_path))

    response = client.get("/logo.png")

    assert response.headers["content-type"] == "image/png"


def test_static_head_request_has_no_charset(tmp_path: Path, test_client_factory: TestClientFactory) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "notes.txt").write_bytes(b"content")
    client = test_client_factory(StaticFiles(directory=tmp_path))

    response = client.head("/notes.txt")

    assert "charset" not in response.headers["content-type"].lower()

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from http.cookies import SimpleCookie

from starlette.requests import Request
from starlette.responses import Response
from starlette.types import Receive, Scope, Send
from tests.types import TestClientFactory

LONG_AGO = dt.datetime(2000, 1, 1, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)


def _expires(header: str, name: str) -> dt.datetime:
    morsel = SimpleCookie(header)[name]
    return parsedate_to_datetime(morsel["expires"])


def test_delete_cookie_expires_in_the_past() -> None:
    response = Response()
    response.delete_cookie("session")

    header = response.headers["set-cookie"]
    morsel = SimpleCookie(header)["session"]
    assert morsel.value == ""
    assert morsel["max-age"] == "0"
    assert _expires(header, "session") < LONG_AGO


def test_delete_cookie_keeps_scope_attributes() -> None:
    response = Response()
    response.delete_cookie("session", path="/admin", domain="example.com", secure=True, httponly=True)

    header = response.headers["set-cookie"]
    morsel = SimpleCookie(header)["session"]
    assert morsel["path"] == "/admin"
    assert morsel["domain"] == "example.com"
    assert morsel["secure"] is True
    assert morsel["httponly"] is True
    assert _expires(header, "session") < LONG_AGO


def test_deleted_cookie_is_dropped_by_client(test_client_factory: TestClientFactory) -> None:
    async def app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        request = Request(scope, receive)
        response = Response("ok", media_type="text/plain")
        if request.cookies.get("session"):
            response.delete_cookie("session")
        else:
            response.set_cookie("session", "abc")
        await response(scope, receive, send)

    client = test_client_factory(app)
    client.get("/")
    assert client.cookies.get("session") == "abc"
    response = client.get("/")
    assert _expires(response.headers["set-cookie"], "session") < LONG_AGO
    assert client.cookies.get("session") is None
